metadata.title: Vidiyum Mun: One Pose, From Spec to Engine
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Vanakkam (Tamil), fits the Chennai setting. Wagwan is Bear-only.
metadata.audience: CSYE 7270 reviewers and makers generating assets for a Godot slice

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN + walker B00. Illustrative reconstruction of the ask (labelled in the topic line), never a transcript. Output lines = the actual built result.
beats.narration_text: Vanakkam, this is Liam, in for Bear. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, not a transcript; the real session was many smaller requests. The shape of it: a time-loop mystery on a Chennai beach, built as a playable Godot slice where every picture and every sound came from a local model.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about Vidiyum Mun, a time-loop mystery at the last party on a fenced beach villa on ECR, Chennai, into a playable 2.5D Godot slice: a 3D marble deck, my hero Hari as generated cel-shaded art in ten states, and generated sound effects and music wired to real game events.
output: Hari: 10 generated states on a 3D deck.
Loop 1 earns the clues. Loop 2 keeps the keys.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW. Misconception 'prompt' corrected to 'pipeline': the body shows the asset is a chain (spec, model, pick, edits, code), not one prompt.
beats.narration_text: One pipeline made Hari, not one prompt. A spec, a model, a pick, three edits, and one function of engine code. Then the night he lives in, played twice, with five sounds that each fire once per event.

props.text:
One prompt made Hari.
A spec, a model, a pick, three edits, one function.
Then one night, looped, scored by five sounds.

beats.role_note: Concept + pillars in plain terms (CONCEPT.md lines 6 and 19-22).
beats.narration_text: Here's the game. You're Hari, a broke engineering student at a rich family's beach party. Every dawn ends in tragedy, and he wakes at eight PM again, keeping only what he learned. Four pillars: see the people nobody sees, every loop you see more, dawn is always coming, and the night belongs to Chennai.

props.excerpt: You are Hari, a broke final-year engineering student at the last party on a rich family's illegally fenced beach on ECR, Chennai. Every dawn something terrible happens and you wake at 8 PM again, so you explore the night, talk to the people the party ignores, and carry what you learn into the next loop to change how dawn arrives.

beats.role_note: Asset trace 1/5: the spec (code-drawn, committed before generation).
beats.narration_text: Step one, the spec, committed before anything was generated. Ten states, and phone is number four: phone to ear, elbow out, eyes slightly away, because he's lying to his mother. The silhouette test found a risk. From the gate, idle, phone and overhear look alike. So the rule is written down: elbow clearly out.

beats.narration_text: Step four, three logged edits. Rembg's anime model cuts out the figure, and the floor shadow goes with the background. A trim to the figure's box. Then a resize to six hundred eighty pixels, padded so the legs, not the phone arm, sit in the centre. My reading: the sprite mirrors around its centre, so his feet stay put when he turns.

beats.role_note: Result of B08 in real play: PHONE → IDLE at call end → WALK → TALK at Krishna.
beats.narration_text: Here's that function at work. The call ends, and phone becomes idle. He walks, and the walk image takes over, flipped or not by direction. At Krishna, talk. One height, feet on the marble. Each state is a single still, so walking is one pose sliding across the deck. That's a trade this slice made on purpose.

beats.role_note: Timeline one-shots. Paired result B11 (real T fast-forward, overhear, 1:40 keys).
beats.narration_text: Now the night. Every timeline event sits behind a flag that resets each loop. When the clock passes one-forty, Advay arrives exactly once. At five-fifty, dawn runs exactly once. Holding T only makes the clock eight times faster. It walks through the same checks, so fast-forward can't skip an event.

beats.role_note: SoundBank listens only. Paired result B13 (recorded test output + this take's counts).
beats.narration_text: Sound only listens. The sound bank connects to the logic's signals and never changes game state. A missing or muted file changes nothing but what you hear. One sound per event is guaranteed upstream, by those flags, so it can be tested without listening.

show.event: line highlight: keys change hands → jingle

props.title: Sound only listens
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/autoload/sound_bank.gd lines 40–46 · build f9d4a611
props.code:
ls.phone_buzz.connect(_play.bind("phone_buzz"))
	ls.clue_saved.connect(func(_id: String) -> void: _play("clue_saved"))
	ls.keys_exchanged.connect(func(_from: String, _to: String) -> void: _play("keys_exchanged"))
	ls.dawn_crash.connect(_on_dawn.bind("dawn_crash"))
	ls.safe_dawn.connect(_on_dawn.bind("safe_dawn"))
	ls.loop_started.connect(func(_index: int) -> void: start_music())
	ls.pause_changed.connect(_on_pause_changed)

beats.role_note: Cause → effect: revision R1 (TEST-REPORT §8). Paired result B18 (before/after screenshots).
beats.narration_text: One cause and effect from the revision log. Early screenshots read as lavender dusk, not one AM. The fix is in these colour stops. The night ambient went down to one-zero-zero-f-two-six, and the moonlight down to zero point zero eight. The deck script raised the string lights to two point eight.

beats.role_note: What was tested and what it doesn't prove (TEST-REPORT §2). RE-VERIFY numbers at freeze.
beats.narration_text: Tested: sound triggers, loop logic, a scene smoke test and the music seams, all passing. Not proven: that a sound is audible or well mixed, or that a loop is musically seamless. The tests jump the clock, so pacing is unchecked. That's what Shriram's own playtest is for.

props.title: What was tested
props.section: TEST-REPORT.md · what these checks do NOT prove
props.excerpt:
The sound test counts requests to SoundBank, not audible output.
The seam check proves there is no sample discontinuity, not that the loop is musically seamless.
The test API jumps the clock (test_advance_to).

beats.role_note: Human vs AI, model per asset, source revision (SOURCES.md, SHRIRAM-DECISIONS.md).
beats.narration_text: Who did what. Shriram wrote the story, the cast and the setting, chose two-and-a-half D, and picked the reference style. Claude wrote the code, prompts, docs and sketches. The models made every asset: FLUX two klein the art, Stable Audio Open the five effects, MusicGen both loops. The build shown is snapshot f 9 d 4.

Shriram: story, characters, setting, tone; 2.5D Telltale style; reference pick B.
Claude: code, prompts, docs, code-drawn sketches; ran the generations.

beats.role_note: Verdict: working / uncertain / known limits / next.
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Working: ten Hari states in a real 3D night, five sounds tied to logic, and one full turn of the loop. Uncertain: whether a first-time player reads the dawn with the sound off. Known limit: overhear still reads like idle from the gate. Next: give overhear its own silhouette, then build loop three.

artifactLines: Works: 10 Hari states in a 3D night, 5 sounds on logic events, one full loop turn.
Uncertain: does a first-time player read the dawn with the sound off?
Known limit: OVERHEAR reads like IDLE at gate distance (FRICTIONAL.md).
Next: give OVERHEAR its own silhouette, then build loop 3.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW: prompt read verbatim, discussed; signs off 'Liam, in for Bear.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. I have a character sheet and one generated reference. For one pose: one, write an edit prompt that keeps identity fixed and changes only the pose clause. Two, name the silhouette risk at my in-game pixel height. Three, list the cleanup steps, and a check that the feet stay put when the sprite flips. It makes Claude reason about your camera before it touches a model. Check its math against a screenshot. Liam, in for Bear.
